image_description: An underwater photograph showing a sea lion swimming in blue-tinted water. The animal is captured in profile, moving from left to right. Its body is streamlined and dark, contrasting with the lighter blue background. One foreflipper is raised high, appearing wing-like, while the hind flippers are extended behind. The head is visible but lacks sharp detail due to water turbidity.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The hind flippers are visible extending from the rear of the body. Their position and shape are consistent with sea lion anatomy (distinct from the fused tail of cetaceans or the sideways orientation of true seals).
Despite the angle, the visible portions of the body suggest standard bilateral symmetry expected in vertebrates. No obvious asymmetrical deformities are visible.

The raised flipper appears slightly elongated and thin at the tip, which could be perspective foreshortening or slight AI warping. It is borderline but worth noting.
